articles.title: 'Hit My Line' — The Walking Dead Star Chandler Riggs Made His Own Resident Evil 7 Fan Film, and He'd Love to Work With Zach Cregger on a Sequel
articles.summary: Chandler Riggs, best known for playing Carl in The Walking Dead, made his own fan film adapting an iconic moment from Resident Evil 7 — and he’d love to collaborate with Zach Cregger on another movie in the RE universe, if he’s up for it.
articles.body:
Chandler Riggs, best known for playing Carl in The Walking Dead, made his own fan film adapting an iconic moment from Resident Evil 7 — and he’d love to collaborate with Zach Cregger on another movie in the RE universe, if he’s up for it.

Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil adaptation hit theaters in September to rave reviews, becoming the most financially successful film in the entire franchise. Just a month later, Riggs is releasing his own Resident Evil short film further along in the games’ timeline in Resident Evil 7: Biohazard.

Riggs adapted the iconic garage fight between Ethan Winters and Jack Baker in a high-octane 20-minute journey, not for fame and acclaim, but merely for the love of the game. Riggs told us that he simply wanted to bring this moment to life on-screen — but given the timing of his film and Cregger’s Resident Evil movie, we had to ask about his thoughts on how close his project was to Cregger’s big-budget take on Capcom’s flagship horror franchise.

Chandler Riggs BIOHAZARD Short Film Behind the Scenes Photos

“We were in pre-production when the article came out that Zack Cregger was going to do his [movie]. I was like, ‘Oh man, all right, we got to get ours out first.’ We were trying to beat the clock and get it out about a month ago, but parts just didn't align that way,” he explained.

“I've been looking forward to [Cregger’s RE movie] for so long,” he added. “And I mean, one of the big reasons I even made this is, you know, I was just dying to see a good, true-to-the-game live-action adaptation of Resident Evil. I cannot wait to see the new one.”

Cregger’s Resident Evil flick was widely well-received, but it has proven divisive among hardcore fans who wished to see a 1:1 adaptation of the games. Cregger was adamantly against doing this, believing the games already told their stories perfectly — and given that Riggs plays the famously faceless Ethan Winters in his own fan film, he was well-aware of how fans might feel about his own take on the source material.

“Look, it's impossible to please everybody, you know?” he admitted. “I think there's always going to be a crowd that is unhappy, but I think that it's a great way to try to get more people into the series, into the franchise, and tell a story that you want to tell. It is not an easy thing; doing a Resident Evil film with Leon and Jill and everyone, that’s a tall order, you know what I mean? Those characters are so iconic from the games, and it's not an uneasy thing to do. So I totally respect going your own direction and doing your own thing.

“It was absolutely an intimidating thing,” he said of playing Ethan Winters, whose face is shown throughout his film. “We're trying to do so much else super faithful and true to the game, but this is a huge aspect that we are breaking from it. But there isn't really another good way to tell [the story] in a live-action format. I was going back and forth like ‘Okay, could we do first person the whole time? Could we avoid getting his face in or anything?’ But the more we went back and forth on it, the more I was like, ‘I mean, if we are going to do this and are going to appeal to a wider audience — more than just the people who played the games — then we're going to have to break those rules. It was very intimidating. Hopefully people are okay with it.”

Riggs is a massive Resident Evil fan, and his fan film is proof of this. Of course, he admitted that he’d love the chance to make a feature-length movie adapting RE7 someday — as well as the chance of working with Zach Cregger on another RE movie, if the director is willing to return to the franchise.

“A huge reason for me even doing this in the first place is that I love being on set and collaborating with cool people, and that's all it is at the end of the day,” he told us. “And just because I want to be on set more, and if I can't be on set doing more films or TV shows or whatever else, then I'll just make it myself. I'll just make it happen. And that's a huge proponent of this. So, if [Cregger] wants to continue in the universe, I'm all for it. Listen, my phone is open. Hit my line!”

It’s possible that this never happens, though, given that Cregger has said he’s never touching a franchise film again due to the strong negative response he received from a vocal portion of the Resident Evil fanbase. That being said, he already has ideas for a sequel , so there’s no telling where the future of RE’s film adaptations lie.

Riggs’ Resident Evil fan film hits the internet on October 14, starring Chandler Riggs as Ethan Winters, Jason Douglas as Jack Baker, Mary Rachel Quinn, Eugenie Bonderant, Johnathan O’Niel, and Sam Coyles.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Street Fighter 6 Reveals Movie Costumes for Zangief, E. Honda and Dhalsim | IGN Fall Fan Fest 2026
articles.summary: Get an exclusive look at the live-action Street Fighter movie costumes for Dhalsim, E. Honda, and Zangief in Street Fighter 6, plus a free Zangief costume code.
articles.body:
The new Street Fighter movie is just days away, and to celebrate, Capcom is releasing a slew of new Street Fighter 6 costumes tied to the film’s release.

The reveals are part of an online scavenger hunt, where a series of movie-related costumes are being unveiled in various places. Guile and M. Bison costumes have already been revealed, and more costumes will be revealed throughout the month.

First up is Dhalsim, who will be played in the new movie by Vidyut Jammwal.

Next, we have a look at E. Honda, portrayed in the film by Hirooki Goto.

Finally, we can reveal the costume for Zangief, played in the movie by Borderlands’ Olivier Richters.

Along with these exclusive images, IGN can reveal the code you can use to redeem your movie-inspired Street Fighter 6 Zangief costume.

You can claim your Zangief code, which is valid across all platforms, starting on October 16. After you do, be sure to check out the Street Fighter movie, which is opening the same day only in theaters.

The Dhalsim and E. Honda costume codes will be revealed soon, so be sure to keep your eyes peeled.

For more IGN Fan Fest , be sure to check out IGN’s website, YouTube, and social channels throughout the week for more than 90 exclusive reveals across games, movies, TV, comics, and collectibles. It all leads to a massive livestream October 14 packed with game announcements, trailers, exclusive clips, celebrity interviews, and more.

articles.title: Batman Star Ben Affleck Says Justice League Reshoots Were the Lowest Point of His Career
articles.summary: Batman actor Ben Affleck has slammed Warner Bros. for how they handled the production of Justice League and called the experience the lowest post of his career.
articles.body:
Batman actor Ben Affleck has slammed Warner Bros. for how they handled the production of Justice League and called the experience the lowest post of his career.

When speaking on the Happy Sad Confused podcast , Affleck was asked about his canceled standalone Batman film, which would've featured Joe Manganiello as Deathstroke . The actor/director said he was excited by what he was cooking up for that Batman film, but admitted that the experience of working on Justice League turned him off to the idea of having to helm a movie in the DC universe.

"The truth is, the experience of Justice League was so, so negative for lots of different reasons," said Affleck. "Some of which having to do with where I was personally, some of which having to do with the tragedy that happened during the time, and also the fact that I really saw how not to make a movie like that when the studio is at odds with the filmmaker. You're really making a mistake. That was what really doomed that."

DCEU Movie Teases That Were Never Paid Off

Affleck is referencing the fact that WB battled director Zack Snyder pretty heavily on his DC films, most notably Justice League after Batman v Superman failed to meet critical expectations. The film was also deemed a bit of a disappointment by WB for not cracking the $1 billion mark, despite featuring three of DC's biggest heroes. As a result, there was a lot of pressure on Snyder to make Justice League more appealing via a lighter tone and different story ideas.

Unfortunately, Snyder had to leave the project during post-production after his daughter took her own life. Warner Bros. then enlisted the help of Avengers director Joss Whedon to come in and direct reshoots, which massively changed the film's tone and story. The reshoots were also hampered by allegations of actors being mistreated by Whedon and other issues, which Affleck stated he was aware of second-hand. He also went on to say that he believes WB used the tragedy in Snyder's family to as an "excuse" to hijack Justice League. He noted that the experience of these reshoots was the "low point" of his career.

"The way in which that was, I thought frankly, used as an excuse was one of the sh**tiest things I'd ever seen," said Affleck. "It was so gross. And then the whole environment and vibe, much of which I wasn't privvy to, but that I sort of heard about second hand in terms of Ray [Fisher] and Gal [Gadot] and other peoples' experiences. It was just like 'Wow, this is about as gross as it gets.'"

Affleck's experience on Justice League was also intertwined with a divorce and issues with alcoholism, leading to a turbulant time for the actor. He eventually stepped down away from the role of Batman and decided not to direct his own Batman film, instead passing the baton over to director Matt Reeves and actor Robert Pattinson. He eventually returned to the role for The Flash, as well as new scenes at the end of Zack Snyder's Justice League, a director's cut of the embattled film.

Zack Snyder also recently stated that a former WB executive expressed regret over how everything was handled . Some hardcore fans have held out hope that maybe one day Snyder's vision will be completed with another Justice League movie, but given how chaotic and negative the experience was for everyone involved, it seems hard to imagine it actually happening.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Jeremy Renner Says the Avengers Will Lose in Doomsday and It's 'Their Fault' Because They 'Didn't Call' Hawkeye
articles.summary: Marvel star Jeremy Renner said the Avengers will lose in Doomsday, and it's "their fault" because they didn't give his Hawkeye a call.
articles.body:
Marvel star Jeremy Renner said the Avengers will lose in Doomsday , and it's "their fault" because they didn't give Hawkeye a call.

The original Avengers star confirmed he wouldn't help fight against Doctor Doom's quest to conquer the multiverse during what appears to be a Q&A segment from last month. In a highlight from the interview, captured and shared on X/Twitter by user @drdoomarchive , Renner confirmed that he's "not in" Avengers: Doomsday when it premieres this December.

That might come as a disappointment for fans of his bow-and-arrow hero, especially considering some of his previous teases suggested he may show up in the Marvel Cinematic Universe again. Alas, it seems his long-awaited return as Hawkeye remains on pause. He doesn't seem too bitter about his absence, but that doesn't mean he isn't willing to take a few jabs at the team.

Hot Toys' Avengers: Doomsday Figures - Image Gallery

"Doomsday, I'm not in," Renner said. "So, the Avengers will probably lose, just so you know."

He added with a laugh, "They didn't call me, so it's their fault they're gonna lose."

Despite lacking Hulk's superpowered strength or the ability to alter reality like Scarlet Witch, Renner's take on Clint Barton has remained a fan-favorite amongst MCU fans since he first appeared as the character in 2011's Thor. He eventually went on to graduate from that cameo role to be a leading hero in projects like the original Avengers, Avengers: Age of Ultron, and Captain America: Civil War, and he eventually led as the main character in Disney+'s 2021 series Hawkeye , too. That said, he's not always shown up for every fight against evil.

Renner infamously sat out 2018's Avengers: Infinity War, which saw its gaggle of heroes and stars truly lose their first fight when Thanos snapped half of the universe into dust. The running joke is, well, if Hawkeye had been around to help, Thanos wouldn't have been so lucky. Now that the character seems to be left out again for Doomsday, Renner can't help but see what's coming.

Of course, he did show up to help finish the fight for the Infinity Stones in Avengers: Endgame, which, coincidentally, saw the heroes win the day (for the most part). Marvel invited fans to revisit that saga-ending story with its Encore re-release last month. Renner said he was excited to see it in theaters at the time.

"They're releasing the Encore of Endgame, I think next week or something, right?" he said. "I'm actually excited to see that. I'm going to take my daughter to see it. She was a little young when it came out prior, so I'm excited that's coming out."

With Renner set to sit out Avengers: Doomsday when it premieres December 18, 2026, we'll have to see if he slips back into his superhero suit for 2027's Avengers: Secret Wars. His future as the character largely remains unclear, though comments he made in 2025 suggested he would be open to returning for Hawkeye Season 2 . Any more from that show, which also starred Hailee Steinfeld as Kate Bishop, seems to be on the back burner for now, though.

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

articles.title: Beats by Dre Teases Pokémon Collaboration With an Electrified Beats Pill Speaker
articles.summary: A six-second video teaser posted to the official Beats by Dre YouTube channel shows the shadow of the Beats Pill speaker, enveloped by animated sparks and flames. The video, titled “Time to catch something new,” ends with an electrified Beats logo next to a Poké Ball.
articles.body:
Beats by Dre has teased an upcoming collaboration with Pokémon.

A six-second video teaser posted to the official Beats by Dre YouTube channel shows the shadow of the Beats Pill speaker, enveloped by animated sparks and flames. The video, titled “Time to catch something new,” ends with an electrified Beats logo next to a Poké Ball.

The teaser video doesn’t offer any product or release date info, but suggests the collaboration will include a Pokémon-branded version of the company’s wireless speaker.

The ‘electric’ animations suggest an unsurprising focus on the Pokémon mascot, Pikachu. To support that theory, unconfirmed images of a bright yellow Pikachu-themed speaker have already started circulating the web. The flaming purple animations point to a possible second product design, potentially inspired by another collaboration favorite, Gengar.

The standard edition of the Beats Pill speaker currently retails for $149.99. We’ll likely get the full reveal of the Pokémon x Beats collaboration alongside a release date in the coming weeks.

Pokémon is celebrating its 30th anniversary this year, giving the biggest franchise in the world the excuse to drop more collaborations than ever. We’ve seen themed hardware from tech companies like Razer , shoe drops from Crocs , and even entire merch collections with retailers like Target .

The amount of buzz going into the Pokémon brand right now would suggest any collab with the gaming giant is an easy win. However, an ongoing scalping crisis in the TCG market continues to bleed into all things Pokémon , with some commenters on the Beats by Dre teaser already deriding the collab as “The beats shill.”

Beats by Dre, which is owned by Apple, launched the first Beats Pill speaker back in 2012. The speaker has gone through a number of upgrades, most recently with a 2024 re-release focused on portability and power.

One thing that hasn't changed is the company's commitment to collaborations. Remember when the Beats Pill popped up in pretty much every YouTube channel? Nowadays, the company focuses on unique themed designs, having recently released product lines with Jennie (of Blackpink fame) and Kim Kardashian.

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

articles.title: Other Mommy’s 4K Steelbook Is Now Up for Preorder – Here’s Where to Buy It
articles.summary: Other Mommy is now available to preorder on 4K, Blu-ray, and as a 4K steelbook. Here's where you can secure a copy ahead of its release.
articles.body:
Spooky season has officially begun, and that means it's time to watch some scary movies. If Other Mommy was on your horror movie watchlist at the cinema this past weekend, and you can't wait to add it to your physical media library, we have good news: preorders for its 4K , Blu-ray , and 4K steelbook are already live at select retailers.

While each of these are available to preorder now, their release date hasn't been announced yet. This is because they've gone up quite early after the film's release (which was just a few days ago ), but don't let the lack of release date stop you from ordering ahead of time. Physical media, like 4Ks and steelbooks, can sell out fast, so be quick to secure your preferred version before that happens.

Other Mommy - Limited Edition Steelbook (4K Ultra HD + Blu-ray + Digital)

As for its design, the steelbook has quite an eerie blue cover, which you can get a closer look at below, with Jessica Chastain's "Other Mommy" facing forward with her arms outstretched. No thanks. And on the inside, you've got an image from the film of Bela screaming in a ball pit, which you can also see below.

Another element of the film's physical release that hasn't been detailed yet because of how early these versions have gone up is bonus features. Once these have been announced, we'll be sure to add them in here as well so you can see what extras will be available to watch alongside the movie.

While Other Mommy hasn't been a critical success , audience's seem to be having a good time with its spooky story as its opening weekend box office results have shown it landing in second place globally with 45.19 million . Its release is certainly well-timed in the lead-up to Halloween, which is good news if you're someone hoping to watch something a little scary at the movie theater this month.

And if you walk away knowing you absolutely need it in your physical media library, you don't have to wait to preorder its 4K, Blu-ray, or steelbook. Treat yourself to it now, and it'll be a nice surprise at your doorstep once it's officially released.

Hannah Hoolihan is a freelancer who writes with the commerce team here at IGN.

articles.title: Miami Vice ‘85 Looks More Like Miami Vice ‘87 in Those First Look Photos
articles.summary: Universal's first look at Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler in Miami Vice ’85 leans closer to late-’80s aesthetics. Read our breakdown of the official photos.
articles.body:
UPDATE : Well, that was hasty of me. My fandom got the better of me and I belted out this reaction to the official Miami Vice ‘85 photos. While the photos show a darker aesthetic and hence my reaction to them outlined below, new behind the scenes photos have emerged online that show Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler looking very much like the TV show’s versions of detectives Ricardo Tubbs and Sonny Crockett, respectively.

Indeed, Butler’s outfit and sunglasses are identical to the style worn by Don Johnson on the classic TV show. So in other words, I’m sorry I ever doubted you, Miami Vice ‘85! Carry on!

If I wanted to see Sonny Crockett wearing a gray suit, I’d watch the Miami Vice movie from 2006 .

Universal released the first official images today of Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler in Miami Vice ‘85 , the upcoming big-screen reboot of the classic NBC television series that helped define the fashion trends of that big-haired decade. At first glance, Miami Vice ‘85 looks cool, sure, but it also looks wrong.

The first two seasons boasted its now iconic pastel color palette, with Don Johnson’s undercover detective Sonny Crockett garbed in expensive designer linen suits of various bright colors (most famously white with a T-shirt underneath). Philip Michael Thomas’ wardrobe as Ricardo Tubbs was always a bit more muted in color, but he almost always wore a double-breasted suit.

But after two seasons of pastels, NBC and the creative team shook things up when Miami Vice returned for its third season in 1986 by embracing a darker color scheme across the board , including in wardrobe. Season 3 also infamously destroyed Crockett’s black convertible Ferrari Daytona Spyder and replaced it with a white Ferrari Testarossa for the final two seasons.

I recount all this because, based on these first look images, Miami Vice ‘85 doesn’t look the way Miami Vice actually did in 1985 when the show was in the tail end of its first season and the start of its second one. That was smack dab in the middle of the show’s legendary pastel phase. That color palette was one of the series’ most talked-about elements. To this day, a movie can do ‘80s pop cultural shorthand by showing a guy in a white suit with a baby blue T-shirt and everyone knows it’s a Miami Vice reference. Hell, GTA: Vice City is a whole homage to the show’s vibe.

The show’s executive producer, Michael Mann, made his 2006 Miami Vice a contemporary tale , understandably dropping the show’s gaudy color palette entirely. The closest Mann’s movie ever came to visually resembling the TV show that spawned it was in its first act when Crockett and Tubbs are dressed in sharp suits, tool around town in a Ferrari, and are undercover inside a nightclub.

Michael B. Jordan is Tubbs. Austin Butler is Crockett. Miami Vice ’85 - now in production. — Miami Vice '85 (@miami_vice85) October 12, 2026

Michael B. Jordan is Tubbs. Austin Butler is Crockett. Miami Vice ’85 - now in production.

So you can imagine my surprise when I see the first look at the new Crockett and Tubbs in Miami Vice ‘85 and they look more like the later seasons’ incarnations of the characters. There’s even a rumor that Crockett will only drive the Testarossa in Miami Vice ‘85 . I know these sound like ridiculous gripes from someone old enough to know better, but, well, fandom gonna fandom. To me it’s no different than people picking apart a new Batman or Spider-Man suit.

Director Joseph Kosinski has spoken at length about how much of a fan he was of the original show growing up , so he certainly knows what he’s doing here in terms of not embracing the pastel aesthetic of 1985. If you’re going to make a period Miami Vice movie, then fans expect to see the iconography of the show in its prime and not from its later seasons when the series went into decline.

Frankly, I’m more hung up on Crockett’s look here than Tubbs’. Tubbs had a beard in later seasons, so that doesn’t really bug me, and I can rationalize the leather trenchcoat Jordan is wearing as being Tubbs’ look when he was still a New York City cop before coming to Miami.

But since Miami Vice ‘85 is adapting the series pilot and some of its first season storylines , that’s all the more reason why lifelong fans like myself expected the new Crockett and Tubbs to look a bit more garish. Maybe they will indeed wear the sort of fashion the show itself made synonymous with the ‘80s, and this is just one muted outfit Crockett wears at some point (nice touch on giving him the gold watch, though, and Crockett and Tubbs’ respective guns look series-accurate).

Like gambling at a craps table, you can’t play scared if you’re going to do a period Miami Vice movie. You have to embrace the gaudiness. It was a greedy, seedy and ambitious era, and the show was essentially a pastel noir. Dammit, Kosinski, I’ve been waiting years for a proper 1980s-set Miami Vice movie. Don’t be afraid to embrace all the elements of the show that you clearly loved, my fellow Gen X-er!

If the director and the studio are worried that people will laugh off a Miami Vice ‘85 movie that actually looked like Miami Vice in 1985, then I wonder why they’re even making it. As a fan, I ask them to heed the words of Don Johnson’s Sonny Crockett: “You just got to learn to go with the heat, Rico. It's just like life. You just gotta keep telling yourself, no matter how hot it gets, sooner or later there's a cool breeze coming in.”

articles.title: Forza Horizon 6 for PS5 Is Up for Preorder - Here's What Comes in Each Edition
articles.summary: Preorders are live for the PS5 version of Forza Horizon 6, and it's even getting a physical edition.
articles.body:
Forza Horizon 6 is set to release for PS5 on January 26. Preorders are live now at all the usual retailers ( see it at Amazon ). This new installment brings the racing action to Japan, in the series’ largest map to date, with all sorts of biomes to explore, ranging from mountaintops to Tokyo streets, and over 550 vehicles to do it in. We gave this game a 10/10 in our review , and the PS5 version promises to be just as good. Read on for details.

If you want a physical version (pour one out for PS5 discs after 2028 ), or a digital copy of the standard edition, you can buy one above. It just comes with the base game and no extras. However, if you preorder the standard edition, you’ll be able to upgrade to the more expensive editions on the PlayStation Store when it comes out on January 26.

The digital deluxe edition comes with the base game, plus the following in-game extras:

The premium edition comes with the base game, plus the following:

Forza Horizon 6 is the latest entry in Microsoft’s open-world racing series from Playground Games. It’s already available for Xbox Series X|S and PC, having released on May 18, 2026. It features over 550 real-life vehicles to collect and spec out. It takes place in Japan, where you can race in all sorts of biomes .

You can build a Valley Estate to buy homes and display your collection of vehicles. You can play solo or co-op or competitively across a campaign filled with all sorts of race types. There are Time Attack Circuits and Drag Meets and stunts to pull off.

In this new era for Microsoft , not all of the company’s first-party games are coming to PS5. Gears of War: E-Day, for instance, is solidly an Xbox exclusive . But thankfully for PS5 owners, Forza Horizon 6 is still heading to Sony’s platform.

It’s one of the premier racing games of the generation, with critic Luke Reilly writing, “Technically, Forza Horizon 6 has not skipped a beat, and it runs like a titan. Aesthetically, it’s the best-looking and best-sounding game Playground has produced to date, set in the most wonderfully realised map it’s ever crafted – full of dense, authentic details and stunning driving roads. It’s rewarding to explore, the campaign is well-paced with a great payoff, and I simply cannot stop playing.”

articles.title: The TCL 27C2A Pro Is Far From MiniLED's Champion
articles.summary: The TCL 272A Pro can impress in testing, but in practice its shortcomings become all the more apparent and it fails to shine nearly as brightly.
articles.body:
The TCL 27C2A Pro is a Mini LED gaming monitor geared to compete with some of the hottest 4K gaming monitors on the market. It offers a 4K panel with quantum dot pixels and a dual-mode that can trade off resolution for speed, much like some other high-end monitors. The TCL 27C2A Pro promises a lot, but its $999 price tag raises a lot of questions.

The TCL 27C2A Pro is a fairly tame monitor with a white-and-black color scheme that seems to chase after either Alienware’s or Samsung’s approval. Other than some RGB lighting, it’s not terribly gaudy, but it’s not incredibly pretty either.

The display squeezes in a 27-inch 4K panel that runs at 160Hz in its native mode or 320Hz when swapped down to 1080p. This kind of dual-mode technology has been popping up on more and more 4K monitors, and it’s great to see as it gives them more flexibility to serve as platforms for AAA titles with gorgeous graphical assets as well as competitive esports games where speed is almost all that matters. The panel features quantum dots and Mini LED backlighting with over 2,300 dimming zones (2,304 to be exact). That gives it a rated 98% coverage of the DCI-P3 color space and rated peak brightness of 2,000 nits — more on that later.

The TCL 27C2A Pro might have a $999 MSRP, but little about the monitor’s constructions feels like it ever should have. It builds on the earlier 27C2A non-pro model, which was cheaper and had fewer dimming zones and a lower peak brightness. But that this more expensive model was built on the bones of a cheap display makes it feel cheap as a result.

The stand and back of the monitor are covered in flimsy plastic. Though, TCL includes some colorful and modestly bright RGB lighting on the back of the monitor that at least makes it look more fun.

The monitor has an adjustable stand that gives you all the height, swivel, tilt, and rotational adjustment you’d expect from a high-end monitor, but it’s terribly jiggly. Any motion to my task transmits up through the stand. Thankfully, the monitor can be placed on a VESA mount.

Rather than having a sturdy, rigid hole through the stand for cable routing, the back of the stand has a little rubber strap that slides down to form a small loop that the cables can go through, but they don’t end up looking super tidy in practice. The monitor also uses an external power brick that you’ll need to find space for on or under your desk.

The monitor gets a couple things right in its design, at least. It includes DisplayPort and two HDMI ports. It also offers a USB-C connection that can handle video input and up to 90W of power output to a connected device. All of the ports can work with the display’s 4K/160Hz peak, though you’ll want to make sure you have cables that can do the job too.

The monitor uses a joystick for controls, which makes navigation easy. The joystick sits front and center underneath the display, so it’s easy to reach.

The TCL 27C2A Pro also includes speakers, but that should be a given in any monitor this expensive. This ensures you always have an option for audio output even when you don’t have headphones or dedicated speakers handy, so it’s a plus.

The TCL 27C2A Pro is a decent monitor for gaming, but it fails to punch up into greatness. It’s sharp and smooth, but not sharper or smoother than others on the block. Its ability to go bright can be handy, especially with its decent anti-glare qualities, but that’s about where its lead ends. Even then, sometimes the monitor just wants to go too dark.

When I tried to watch Dune, every dark scene just sank into too much darkness, leaving it hard to see anything despite the monitor’s very bright capabilities. The same happened while watching Avatar 2, with most of the movie bright and lovely but the final night of action growing incredibly dim. A few hours of Assassin’s Creed Shadows went well enough, but when I accidentally took out all the lights in a tower while fighting, suddenly I could hardly see what was on screen to make it through the combat. With local dimming, small bright elements can just about vanish on the display, too. My mouse cursor moving across a black screen dims considerably, and starfields look awful.

The TCL 27C2A Pro hits its stride when displaying bright and colorful content. Hades 2 sings, rendered in sharp fidelity and running smoothly. There’s not enough ghosting to be a bother in this game, and the color simply glows out of the monitor. There’s still some annoying artifacts from local dimming, such as certain elements (like the coin counter) appearing dim when it’s in an otherwise dark section of the screen, but these are generally subtle and hard to notice.

As things turn darker or rely more on contrast for effect, the MiniLED tech’s shortcomings next to OLED become obvious. In areas of strong contrast, such as a black and white box next to each other, exhibit a haze where the local dimming overlaps with one of the areas, dimming a portion of what should be bright white. White text on a black background can appear dim and unevenly lit. That’s rough for captions. In bright scenes, the Mini LED backlighting can definitely deliver, but black pixels close to bright elements get lifted so the actual contrast in that area will fall back to typical IPS levels. In the end, the visual quality is simply too situational.

Next to an OLED display, the differences really stand out. The whole image on the TCL 27C2A Pro is simply flattened. Little details that pop on OLED don’t have that effect on the TCL 27C2A Pro in many cases, and it’s because the contrast is neutered right where a detail should be emphasized because of the light doing the popping. This can leave things simply looking a little washed out.

Then there’s the matter of the dual-mode settings. The 4K/160Hz mode looks good, but the monitor can drop down to 1080p/320Hz for faster visuals. I saw this type of tech in action on the Asus ROG Swift OLED PG27UCWM , and it worked quite well there. Going down in resolution that much is always going to hurt a little, but the TCL 27C2A Pro looked particularly soft, with even decently sized text almost appearing blurry. It wasn’t too dramatic in the throes of battle in Hades 2, but when stopping to enjoy the scenery or read dialogue, it was more of a bother.

The TCL 27C2A Pro is capable of putting up some terribly impressive numbers when tested with a colorimeter, though. I measured its color gamut at 100% of the sRGB and 99% of the DCI-P3 color spaces. That’s just what you should expect from quantum dot color. The monitor defaults to 50% brightness, which hits a modest 167.8 nits, but if you dial it up to max brightness, it soars up to 570 nits. The wide color gamut and brightness don’t guarantee excellent visual performance in all conditions, though.

At full brightness, it achieved a 5,930:1 contrast ratio, which sounds great on paper, but the use of local dimming zones, even if there are over 2,300 of them, means the contrast depends in part on where it’s being measured. A subsequent test saw the monitor reach 8,150:1 likely due simply to a small shift in colorimeter placement. With bright squares in each corner, I even measured perfect black at the center of the display, giving it infinite contrast. But if I move the colorimeter closer to the corners, suddenly black pixels can have a few tenths of a nit bleeding through. With a 6x4 checkboard, the monitor manages a much tamer 2,038:1 contrast ratio with HDR white measuring at 693 nits and black measuring at 0.34 nits.

HDR has a lot of benefits for the monitor. It continues to cover the broad 99% coverage of the DCI-P3 colorspace alongside a comfortable 6500K whitepoint, and it can simply blast light out of a big enough area. Both a 10% window and a full white screen hit a little over 2,000 nits. That’s where its edge over OLED lies, as OLED monitors are lucky to hit half that for a 10% window and a quarter of that for a full white screen. Even a 1% window hit 975 nits. That said, smaller HDR highlights (e.g., muzzle flares or stars) will either lack brightness or lift the brightness of surrounding pixels.

The speakers on the monitor are kind of boxy and unpleasant. They put out respectable volume for casual listening, but won’t sound great for music or games, especially where spatial sound is concerned. After gaming on them for a while, they really started to grate on my ears. So, trust me, use a gaming headset.

Mark Knapp is a contributing freelancer for IGN covering everything electronics and gaming hardware. He has over 10 years of experience in the tech industry with bylines at PCMag, Reviewed, CNET, and more. Find Mark on Twitter @Techn0Mark or BlueSky at @Techn0Mark .

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE: For the Stars Images Showcase the Upcoming Space Sandbox Survival Multiplayer Game | IGN Fall Fan Fest 2026

articles.body:
As part of IGN Fan Fest 2026: Fall Edition, we are proud to reveal five brand-new screenshots of For the Stars, Snail Games USA's upcoming space sandbox survival game that will have you exploring and settling planets, uncovering the secrets of alien civilizations, and much more.

The images, which you can see below, show off some of For The Stars' different biomes, weapons, flora and fauna, vehicles, spaceships, and more. They also offer a glimpse into the multiplayer experience that allows friends to explore this universe together.

Players will be traveling from planet to planet and establishing outposts to upgrade their tech, studying alien artifacts and natural phenomena, and surviving any challenges that come their way in an effort to get more powerful and "explore further into the unknown."

Speaking of outposts, players will need to balance the needs of each area with proper laboratories, factories, and living quarters. Spacecraft will also need to be upgraded, and they can be customized to make them unique and suited for any task ahead.

And yes, friends can come along for the ride. Collaborate on building projects, share different discoveries, and work together to overcome any obstacle. Furthermore, Snail Games USA teases that players can "choose to enter contested regions to fight other players for control of the galaxy."

articles.title: The Tiny XTEINK X4 Pro Ebook Reader Is on Sale for Its Lowest-Ever Price
articles.summary: The tiny XTEINK X4 Pro packs all the features you'd want in an ebook reader into an easily pocketable device, and it's on sale now at Amazon.
articles.body:
Our world is increasingly filled with colorful, glowing screens it can be hard to take your eyes off of. If you would like to decrease your screen time, you might also want to increase your reading time. One of the most convenient ways to do that is to use a tiny e-book reader like the XTEINK X4 Pro, currently on sale at Amazon for $84.15 (down from $99). It’s a limited-time deal, so it could vanish at any time. Let’s look at what this little device can do.

The XTEINK X4 Pro is a tiny, easily pocketable e-book reader; it's 5.95mm thin and weighs just 72 grams. The e-ink display measures 4.3 inches diagonally, which is big enough to read without straining your eyes. But the whole device is barely bigger than a credit card. It can even magnetically snap onto the back of your phone.

It has most of the features you’d expect in an ebook reader in 2026. It has a dual-tone front light so you can read in low-light (or no-light) situations. The e-ink display is easy to read in direct sunlight, just like the pages of a paper book. It has both touchscreen and physical buttons to turn pages forward and back. And because e-ink displays require very little power, a single charge lasts weeks.

Format-wise, it supports EPUB, TXT, MOBI, PDF formats. You can load books onto it using the official app, the cloud, or a microSD card. The app can even convert ebooks from different formats into a format viewable on the device.

It has buttons for home, power on/off, next page, and previous page. It has a microSD card slot and a lanyard hole. It doesn’t come with a charging cable, but it does include an adapter that lets you use a USB-C charging cable to charge it using a magnet to attach it to your device. It also comes with a magnet ring you can stick to the back of the device to make it snap to the back of your phone.

Once you go into the settings, you’ll find this thing is super customizable. You can change the functions of the buttons. You can adjust things like the font, line spacing, text size, and brightness. You can go into night mode, and even set a color temperature to trigger on and off automatically at certain times of day.

Personally, I love reading paper books, but I have to admit they’re not the most convenient things in the world to haul around, especially if you don’t want to bring a bag where you’re going. Even a Kindle is too big to carry on your person. That’s where a device like this fits in, so you can carry a book (or folder full of books) with you wherever you go, even in the same pocket as your phone.

I also like the small screen size, because it limits the number of words on a page. Sometimes, when I’m reading a textbook or a big hardcover, I find the wall of text on the page visually unappealing, especially if the print is small. I look at a page like that, and think, “I’m never going to read all that” – and I was an English major. On the XTEINK X4 Pro, you’ll never have an intimidating amount of text on the screen.

The best part about it is the size. Because it's so pocketable, you can just bring it with you anywhere you go. Then, when you find yourself in a situation where you'd normally pull out your phone and start doomscrolling, you can pull out the X4 Pro instead and read a few pages in whatever book you're currently reading.

articles.title: Breaking Bad Star RJ Mitte Dead at 34
articles.summary: RJ Mitte, the actor best known for playing Walter White Jr. in Breaking Bad, has died at 34.
articles.body:
RJ Mitte, the actor best known for playing Walter White Jr. in Breaking Bad, has died at 34.

TMZ reported that a county official in Texas confirmed the news that he died today, October 12, 2026. The site stated it was told that Mitte died by suicide.

Additional details surrounding his death are unclear. An investigation is ongoing.

Mitte started his career in Hollywood with a small role in Disney's Hannah Montana before appearing as the son of Bryan Cranston's Walter White when Breaking Bad premiered in 2008. He played Walter 'Flynn' White Jr. for 56 episodes, cementing him not only as one of the AMC show's most prominent characters, but one of the more recognizable characters in TV history.

Mitte appeared in all five seasons of Breaking Bad but went on to have an acting career that saw him contribute to different mediums across the entertainment spectrum. In 2013, he showed up in a music video for Steel Panther's "Party Like Tomorrow Is The End of the World." In 2014, he appeared in nine episodes of the television series Switched at Birth.

While his time on TV screens saw him also play roles in things like Now Apocalypse and This Close, his movie resume included parts in things like 2021's Triumph, 2020's The Oak Room, and 2019's All the Little Things We Kill. His most recent project saw him star as Joshua in this year's Talking to Stranger.

Representatives for Mitte shared a statement with TMZ confirming the passing. They called him a "beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate."

"RJ Mitte was best known for his role as Walter 'Flynn' White Jr. on AMC’s critically acclaimed, award-winning series Breaking Bad," the message continued. "Drawing from his own experience living with cerebral palsy, Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built a platform on disability awareness and inclusion. Beyond entertaining friends and family around the world, he served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children’s."

Fans of Mitte's work have already taken to social media to share their condolences. Others are taking the time to remember his impact not only as an actor but also as an important disability rights advocate.

If you or someone you know is thinking of suicide, please call the 24/7 National Suicide Prevention Lifeline by dialing 988 or go to SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources .

articles.title: Nintendo Was Reportedly Unhappy With Elon Musk's Saturday Night Live Wario Sketch
articles.summary: Nintendo was reportedly unhappy with Elon Musk's 2021 Saturday Night Live sketch where he played Wario.
articles.body:
Nintendo was reportedly unhappy with Elon Musk's 2021 Saturday Night Live sketch where he played Wario.

In 2021, Elon Musk starred in a Saturday Night Live sketch where he played Wario. The nefarious Nintendo character took the stand in a courtroom, where he was being accused of murdering everyone's favorite plumber, Mario. The skit was poorly received online and, apparently, by Nintendo itself. Kit Ellis and Krysta Yang, two former Nintendo PR managers, revealed in a recent episode of their YouTube show that the SNL skit "did not go well" with Nintendo at the time.

The two got on the subject following the recent Saturday Night Live sketch where The Legend of Zelda protagonist Link and GTA 6's Jason Duvall debated each other over who would have the better game. The sketch largely pokes fun at The Legend of Zelda while trying to make GTA 6 seem like the "cooler" game, which itself led to some mixed reactions online. Nevertheless, Ellis and Yang think that it probably went over better than Musk's sketch.

The two recalled being at Nintendo when the skit aired and stated that it was "not beloved." Ellis went on to note that the sketch was also oddly timed, as there wasn't even a new Wario game or product when it happened. He went on to say that the sketch also pushed into "uncomfortable" for Nintendo, likely referencing some of the more risque jokes in the skit. The SNL crew made jokes about Mario using cocaine, Luigi sleeping with Princess Peach, and featured a video of Luigi's censored penis. It was... interesting, to say the least.

Naturally, it's understandable if Nintendo wasn't thrilled about its family-friendly characters being portrayed as sexual deviants. SNL has parodied Nintendo a number of other times, including a sketch featuring a dark and gritty version of Mario Kart , heavily inspired by HBO's adaptation of The Last of Us.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Will You Get a Paramount+ Subscription to Watch Avatar: Seven Havens?
articles.body:
Avatar: Seven Havens premiered last week, exclusively on Paramount+. And shortly after that happened, Paramount went ahead and revealed that seasons 3 and 4 of the series are already greenlit alongside another Avatar project.

As someone who doesn't currently have a Paramount+ subscription , I find myself conflicted. Avatar: The Last Air Bender is my favorite animated show of all time and I loved what the creators did with The Legend of Korra as well. So while I really want to watch Seven Havens, I don't really want to add a Paramount+ subscription to my monthly streaming bill.

I could have easily written off the new show as a shameless grab for my subscription dollars, but the very positive reviews of the premiere make it it harder to avoid. Pair that with the fact that I still haven't seen the Avatar Aang movie yet, and it seems inevitable that I'm going to get at least a temporary subscription just to watch those two things.

The good news is that the release schedule for Avatar: Seven Havens is actually pretty condensed. There are 13 episodes in season 1, but they are all releasing in batches. The final four episodes are currently set to be added to the service on October 30. So if you sign up for a one-month subscription now, you should be able to finish the series before you cancel.

Avatar: Seven Havens Episode Title Reveals

Paramount+ used to offer a free trial, but they decided to drop that at the beginning of the year when they began adding UFC fights to the platform. That being said, there is a free trial of sorts available if you choose to take the Walmart+ route. If you haven't used it already, you can currently sign up for 30 days for $1, which happens to include access to basic Paramount+ subscription.

With the Paramount Skydance acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery now complete , this is likely not the last time a Paramount+ subscription will be needed to watch a popular show. For now I'm still clinging to my HBO Max, Hulu, and Disney+ bundle as my main source of content, but who knows when that could go away. For now I'm glad I only have to spend an extra $8.99 to watch the new Avatar show.

articles.title: Yelich's huge two-run hit gives Brewers lead, drives out Yamamoto
articles.summary: After Jake Bauers worked a 12-pitch walk to load the bases, Christian Yelich hit a two-run single to give the Brewers a 3-2 lead in the third inning.
articles.body:
What a third inning and what a moment for the Milwaukee Brewers .

After falling behind the Los Angeles Dodgers , 2-1, in the top of the inning, they took the lead, 3-2, in the bottom with a big hit from their captain.

Christian Yelich hit a two-out single with the bases loaded to drive in two runs and drive Dodgers starter Yoshi Yamamoto out of the game. Yamamoto threw 36 pitches in the inning alone and finished with 75.

Yelich got the glory but the absolute star of the inning was Jake Bauers, who worked a 12-pitch walk that seemed to build with every delivery.

A couple were pop-ups that Dodgers defenders couldn't quite chase down in foul territory, and Bauers wound up getting on base to load them up.

It's the most pitches Yamamoto has thrown in any MLB appearance in his career.

Brewers vs Dodgers highlights, National League Championship Series Game 2

To start the inning, David Hamilton singled, Jackson Chourio flew out, Brice Turang walked – despite another pitch that would have been strike three if the Dodgers had asked for an ABS replay – and William Contreras flew out. All the at-bats were lengthy.

That brought up Bauers, followed by Yelich, who didn't have a single playoff RBI dating to Game 7 of the 2018 series before getting three now this year.

articles.title: Rays In ALCS, Brewers In NLCS Hold 2026 Statistical Edges
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers hold statistical edges in their 2026 ALCS and NLCS matchups. Not surprising as both compiled the best records in eac...
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers hold statistical edges in their respective 2026 ALCS and NLCS matchups. Not surprising, since they both compiled the best records in each league.

What is a surprise, as pointed out by Forbes.com Senior Contributor Barry M. Bloom , is that three lower-payroll clubs are still alive. The combined 2026 payrolls of Milwaukee, Tampa Bay and the Cleveland Guardians of $360.5 million is well behind the Los Angeles Dodgers' hefty $433 million payroll .

The Rays finished 98-64 for the best record in the American League. In their ALCS matchup against the Cleveland Guardians , they held a regular-season advantage in 33 of 45 statistical matchups with one tie. Each club had 58 batters hit by pitches during the regular season.

Cleveland won the AL Central with an 85-77 record, one game better than the Chicago White Sox. Chicago swept the AL West champion Houston Astros, 2-0, in a wild-card matchup and took a 2-0 lead over Cleveland in the AL Division Series. Then Jose Ramirez's hitting helped the Guardians win three in a row to advance to the ALCS.

The Brewers' 103-59 record led the National League. Their NLCS matchup against Los Angeles is closer, according to regular-season stats. Milwaukee had better numbers in 27 of 45 categories.

The defending two-time World Series champion Dodgers won the AL West at 100-62, nine games ahead of the San Diego Padres, then beat the Atlanta Braves in a four-game NLDS. The Braves had edged the Philadelphia Phillies in a three-game wild-card series.

San Diego swept the Chicago Cubs, 2-0, in the wild card, then fell to Milwaukee in a four-game NLDS.

Let's look at regular-season numbers for the remaining four teams, keeping in mind that numbers do not always tell a complete story. The Dodgers and Guardians are out to prove Mark Twain correct. The writer would obviously not be a fan of analytics as he often wrote: "There are three kinds of lies: lies, damned lies, and statistics."

The Rays won the season series, 5-1, outscoring Cleveland, 20-8. Five of the games were close, however. Three of the Tampa Bay wins were shutouts as the Guardians batted only .170 against Rays pitchers. Tampa Bay hit .242 in the six games.

The Guardians' lone win was at home, 3-1, on April 29 as Gavin Williams allowed only an earned run over 7 1/3 innings, striking out nine without a walk. Chase DeLauter had a two-run single among Cleveland's nine hits.

The only blowout was the Rays' 11-3 win at home on July 24. Ryan Vilade hit a two-run homer off Cleveland starter Joey Cantillo and former Guardian Richie Palacios had a three-run homer off Hunter Gaddis. Catcher Nick Fortes went 4-for-4 while Chandler Simpson, Cedric Mullins and Jonny Deluca all had two hits for the Rays.

Shane McClanahan got the win. The lefty starter has not pitched since Sept. 3 and is not on the playoff roster due to a forearm injury.

The Brewers won three of four in Los Angeles to take the season series, 4-3. The Dodgers dominated most head-to-head stats, thanks to 11-3 and 5-1 wins in Milwaukee.

Milwaukee pitching was ghastly in the 11-3 loss at Miller Park on May 23, allowing 11 walks and 10 hits, five of them for extra bases. Teoscar Hernandez had six RBI for the Dodgers on a three-run homer and two singles. Roki Sasaki and four relivers combined to strike out 11 Brewers – Jackson Chourio and Jake Bauers three times apiece.

Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski fanned six over six innings in a 4-1 win at Dodger Stadium on Aug. 15, putting his record at 12-5. William Contreras and Joey Ortiz each hit two-run homers.

Overall in the regular-season matchups, Milwaukee had the better batting average, .228 to .188, but the Dodgers had more power with 7 homers, 6 doubles and 3 triples to the Brewers' 3 homers, 9 doubles and 0 triples.

The Guardians send left-hander Foster Griffin (15-6, 3.60 ERA) to the mound against Rays right-hander Drew Rasmussen (16-5, 2.67 ERA).

Griffin was great in his first playoff outing, fanning seven over 2 2/3 innings of relief in Chicago in Cleveland's must-win Game 3. Acquired at the trade deadline from Washington, he went 3-3 with a 5.19 ERA in nine starts for Cleveland. He was 12-3 with a 3.06 ERA in 22 starts for the Nationals in his return to MLB after three years in Japan.

In one start against the Dodgers for Washington, he gave up one run over five innings in a no-decision, walking five, fanning six.

Rasmussen flirted with a no-hitter in a tense 1-0 win over the New York Yankees in Game 1 of the AL Division Series. In eight innings, he walked two, struck out 10 and gave up only a two-out double to Austin Wells in the eighth.

Against Cleveland in 2026, Rasmussen went 1-1 with a 1.50 ERA in two starts, striking out 15 over 12 innings. The loss was in Cleveland when he gave up three runs (two earned) over five innings.

It will be tough to match the intensity of Milwaukee's 2-1 win Sunday night in Game 1 of the NLCS. Cleveland's long-suffering fans will be ready to roar, however, as they will try to cheer their underdog team to a quick start.

Only the Dodgers among the four remaining teams have won a World Series since Cleveland last prevailed way back in 1948. The team made it back but lost in 1954, 1995, 1997 and 2016.

The Milwaukee Brewers are trying to get back to a second World Series, losing in 1982. The Rays are seeking their third Series, losing in 2008 and 2020. The Dodgers are trying to return for a chance to be the first ballclub to win it all three times in a row since the Yankees in 1998, 1999 and 2000.
